## Simulations Directory

### Horizontal Spring

- **URL**: https://physicshub.github.io/simulations/HorizontalSpring
- **Description**: A spring attached to the left wall with a draggable mass. Explore Hooke's Law and oscillation on a horizontal plane — approachable from middle school, standard in high school.

### Double Pendulum

- **URL**: https://physicshub.github.io/simulations/DoublePendulum
- **Description**: Simulate a double pendulum and explore chaotic motion. Watch how small changes in initial conditions lead to completely different trajectories — a classic university-level example of chaos theory.
- **Target Level**: undergraduate
- **Difficulty**: advanced
- **Physics Topics**: [object Object], [object Object], [object Object]

### 1D Collision simulation

- **URL**: https://physicshub.github.io/simulations/CollisionSimulation
- **Description**: Simulate 1D elastic collisions with velocity vectors, momentum, and kinetic energy visualization — a core momentum topic in high-school physics.

- **Physics Topics**: [object Object], [object Object]

### Pi From Collisions

- **URL**: https://physicshub.github.io/simulations/PiCollisions
- **Description**: Simulate two colliding blocks of different masses to derive pi. A beautiful conservation-law puzzle for university students (and gifted high-schoolers): adjust the mass of the larger block by a power of 100 to see further precision of pi.
- **Target Level**: undergraduate
- **Difficulty**: extended
- **Physics Topics**: [object Object], [object Object], [object Object]
- **Related Guide**: [Read Guide](https://physicshub.github.io/blog/pi-from-block-collisions-explained)

### Trigonometric Circle

- **URL**: https://physicshub.github.io/simulations/TrigonometricCircle
- **Description**: Interactive unit circle with a draggable angle θ. Visualize sin, cos, tan, cot, sec and csc as circle segments, watch the generalized wave A·sin(ωθ+φ) plot in real time, and trace the inverse functions arcsin, arccos, arctan and arccot — a bridge from middle-school geometry to high-school trig.
- **Target Level**: lowerSecondary
- **Difficulty**: core
- **Physics Topics**: [object Object], [object Object]

### Vectors: components, addition, dot and cross products

- **URL**: https://physicshub.github.io/blog/comprehensive-guide-to-vector-operations
- **Summary**: A vector carries a magnitude and a direction. Split it into components and the algebra falls out: addition, scaling, the dot product for angles, the cross product for area and torque.

### How does a ball accelerate toward a target?

- **URL**: https://physicshub.github.io/blog/ball-uniformly-accelerated-motion
- **Summary**: Acceleration is how fast velocity changes. Point a constant acceleration at a target and the ball speeds up, overshoots, then loops back — here is why, with a simulation to try.
- **Date Published**: 21/01/2026

### Free Fall & Air Resistance: Interactive Physics Simulation Guide

- **URL**: https://physicshub.github.io/blog/ball-free-fall-comprehensive-guide
- **Summary**: Explore how gravity, air resistance, and wind affect a falling ball. Interactive simulations and clear explanations covering free fall, drag force, and planetary gravity — from beginner to advanced.
- **Date Published**: 24/01/2026

### How does a spring work?

- **URL**: https://physicshub.github.io/blog/spring-connection
- **Summary**: A spring pushes back in proportion to how far you stretch it — that is Hooke's law, and it is exactly what makes a mass on a spring oscillate. Here is the physics, with a simulation.
- **Date Published**: 21/01/2026

### The Physics of the Pendulum: This is How It Works

- **URL**: https://physicshub.github.io/blog/physics-of-pendulum-explained
- **Summary**: An exhaustive exploration of pendulum dynamics from elementary observations to advanced nonlinear analysis, encompassing simple harmonic motion, energy conservation, chaotic behavior, and quantum mechanical interpretations.
- **Date Published**: 26/01/2026

### How does projectile motion work?

- **URL**: https://physicshub.github.io/blog/projectile-parabolic-motion
- **Summary**: Gravity pulls a projectile straight down while its sideways speed stays constant. Those two independent motions combine into a parabola — here is the maths, with an interactive launcher.
- **Date Published**: 21/01/2026

### The Three-Body Problem: The Equation That Broke Physics

- **URL**: https://physicshub.github.io/blog/physics-behind-three-body-problem
- **Summary**: Two bodies orbiting under gravity are perfectly predictable; three are chaotic. Why the three-body problem has no formula — and what the Netflix show gets right and wrong.
- **Date Published**: 20/04/2026

### How Two Sliding Blocks Compute π — The Most Surprising Result in Physics

- **URL**: https://physicshub.github.io/blog/pi-from-block-collisions-explained
- **Summary**: Two frictionless blocks and a wall, all collisions elastic: count the clacks and you get the digits of π. The physics behind it, from the first collision to the geometric proof.
- **Date Published**: 02/06/2026
